discovery: Prediction and discovery of flat bands, correlated insulators and superconductivity in magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene

nominees.name: Allan H. MacDonald
nominees.affiliation: University of Texas at Austin, USA

subfield: Condensed matter physics: two-dimensional materials and correlated electrons
motivation: Bistritzer and MacDonald predicted in 2011 that twisting two graphene sheets to a 'magic angle' near 1.1 degrees makes the Dirac bands nearly flat. Jarillo-Herrero developed the tear-and-stack technique that controls the twist angle precisely. In 2018 his group used it to show, in clean transport experiments, that magic-angle bilayer graphene hosts correlated insulating states and unconventional superconductivity, all tuned with a simple electrostatic gate. The discovery turned the twist angle into a new control parameter and started the field of moiré quantum matter. Research groups around the world have since observed ferromagnetism, the quantum anomalous Hall effect and, in moiré semiconductors and rhombohedral graphene, fractional quantum anomalous Hall states at zero magnetic field. A clear theoretical prediction, an ingenious device method and unambiguous measurements together opened a highly tunable platform for strongly correlated and topological physics.
